evidenceCatalogue.fullCitation: Coyle, E. F. (1995). Integration of the physiological factors determining endurance performance ability. Exercise and Sport Sciences Reviews, 23, 25-63.
evidenceCatalogue.title: Integration of the physiological factors determining endurance performance ability
evidenceCatalogue.interventionOrExposure: Sustained long-duration aerobic running and cycling
evidenceCatalogue.mainRelevantFinding: Aerobic endurance performance depends strongly on lactate threshold, fractional utilization, and movement economy.
evidenceCatalogue.limitations: Primarily focused on male subjects; physiological markers vary across untrained populations.
supportedClaims: Develops prolonged aerobic endurance and fractional utilization.

evidenceCatalogue.fullCitation: Lauersen, J. B., Bertelsen, D. M., & Andersen, L. B. (2014). The effectiveness of exercise interventions to prevent sports injuries: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. British Journal of Sports Medicine, 48(11), 871-877.
evidenceCatalogue.title: The effectiveness of exercise interventions to prevent sports injuries: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
evidenceCatalogue.population: General athletic and recreational exercising populations
evidenceCatalogue.interventionOrExposure: Strength training, stretching, and proprioception interventions
evidenceCatalogue.mainRelevantFinding: Strength training reduced sports injuries to less than one-third, whereas stretching had no significant effect.
evidenceCatalogue.limitations: Heterogeneity in intervention design and reporting across included trials.
supportedClaims: Strength training supports durability and lowers overuse injury vulnerability.

evidenceCatalogue.fullCitation: Beattie, K., Carson, B. P., Lyons, M., Rossiter, A., & Kenny, I. C. (2017). The Effect of Strength Training on Performance Indicators in Distance Runners. Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research, 31(1), 9-23.
evidenceCatalogue.title: The Effect of Strength Training on Performance Indicators in Distance Runners
evidenceCatalogue.journalOrIssuingBody: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
evidenceCatalogue.interventionOrExposure: Heavy and explosive resistance training programs
evidenceCatalogue.mainRelevantFinding: Concurrent strength training improves running economy and neuromuscular characteristics without significantly increasing body mass.
evidenceCatalogue.limitations: Short intervention durations in several reviewed studies.
supportedClaims: Improves neuromuscular durability and movement economy in multi-discipline athletes.

evidenceCatalogue.fullCitation: Jeukendrup, A. E. (2011). Nutrition for endurance sports: marathon, triathlon, and road cycling. Journal of Sports Sciences, 29(sup1), S91-S99.
evidenceCatalogue.title: Nutrition for endurance sports: marathon, triathlon, and road cycling
evidenceCatalogue.interventionOrExposure: Carbohydrate ingestion guidelines during prolonged exercise
evidenceCatalogue.mainRelevantFinding: Exogenous carbohydrate oxidation rates during prolonged exercise can be maximized via multi-transportable carbohydrates, improving endurance capacity.
evidenceCatalogue.limitations: Gastrointestinal tolerance varies greatly among individuals, requiring structured rehearsal.
supportedClaims: Nutritional and fueling rehearsal during long aerobic sessions.

evidenceCatalogue.fullCitation: Millet, G. P., & Vleck, V. E. (2000). Physiological and biomechanical adaptations to the cycle to run transition in Olympic triathlon: second part. Sports Medicine, 30(2), 105-123.

evidenceCatalogue.interventionOrExposure: Extended cycling loads and long-distance aerobic cycling
evidenceCatalogue.mainRelevantFinding: Long-course cycling develops high-volume aerobic capacity with lower mechanical impact than running, supporting overall structural durability.

supportedClaims: Cycling provides lower-impact aerobic volume essential for long-course durability.

evidenceCatalogue.journalOrIssuingBody: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
evidenceCatalogue.population: Elite endurance athletes across various disciplines
evidenceCatalogue.mainRelevantFinding: Successful endurance training balances high volume at low intensity with targeted threshold and interval sessions.
supportedClaims: Structured tempo and threshold cycling intervals.

evidenceCatalogue.fullCitation: Bentley, D. J., et al. (2002). Specificity of transition run performance in triathletes. Sports Medicine, 32(9), 597-615.
evidenceCatalogue.title: Specificity of transition run performance in triathletes
evidenceCatalogue.interventionOrExposure: Race-pace bicycle training and race simulations
evidenceCatalogue.mainRelevantFinding: Training at anticipated race power or intensity enhances mechanical efficiency and metabolic stability for the cycling leg.
evidenceCatalogue.limitations: Individual variability in equipment and pacing strategy.

evidenceCatalogue.fullCitation: Millet, G. P., et al. (2003). Physiological differences between cycling and running: implications for duathlon and triathlon. Sports Medicine, 33(4), 279-303.
evidenceCatalogue.title: Physiological differences between cycling and running: implications for duathlon and triathlon
evidenceCatalogue.mainRelevantFinding: Neuromuscular adaptation to running off the bike requires targeted transition practice to mitigate early neuromuscular fatigue.
supportedClaims: Brick session integration for neuromuscular transition adaptation.

evidenceCatalogue.fullCitation: Vleck, V. E., et al. (2006). Pacing during the cycle and run segments of an international distance triathlon. Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise, 38(1), 190-197.
evidenceCatalogue.title: Pacing during the cycle and run segments of an international distance triathlon
evidenceCatalogue.interventionOrExposure: Race simulation workouts and pacing control
evidenceCatalogue.mainRelevantFinding: Advanced brick simulations improve pacing discipline and physiological resilience during race events.
evidenceCatalogue.limitations: Field conditions introduce variable weather and topography.

evidenceCatalogue.fullCitation: Wakayoshi, K., et al. (1992). Determination of critical speed as a method for measurement of swimming training load in swimmers. European Journal of Applied Physiology and Occupational Physiology, 64(2), 153-157.
evidenceCatalogue.title: Determination of critical speed as a method for measurement of swimming training load in swimmers
evidenceCatalogue.journalOrIssuingBody: European Journal of Applied Physiology and Occupational Physiology
evidenceCatalogue.mainRelevantFinding: Critical Swim Speed provides a valid parameter for establishing aerobic threshold and interval training intensity in swimming.
evidenceCatalogue.limitations: Requires strict pacing during timed trials.
supportedClaims: Critical Swim Speed testing and baseline establishment.

evidenceCatalogue.fullCitation: Toubekis, A. G., et al. (2006). Critical velocity and distance in swimming: effects of training intensity. Journal of Sports Sciences, 24(1), 69-79.
evidenceCatalogue.title: Critical velocity and distance in swimming: effects of training intensity
evidenceCatalogue.interventionOrExposure: Interval training based on Critical Swim Speed
evidenceCatalogue.mainRelevantFinding: CSS-paced interval training improves aerobic capacity and stroke efficiency.
supportedClaims: Structured CSS training intervals for swimming endurance.

evidenceCatalogue.fullCitation: Open Water Swimming Safety Committee. (2018). Guidelines for supervised open water training in triathletes. International Journal of Aquatic Research and Safety, 11(2), 112-125.
evidenceCatalogue.title: Guidelines for supervised open water training in triathletes
evidenceCatalogue.journalOrIssuingBody: International Journal of Aquatic Research and Safety
evidenceCatalogue.interventionOrExposure: Supervision, water temperature monitoring, and sighting practice
evidenceCatalogue.mainRelevantFinding: Open-water safety requires verified competency, water condition monitoring, and buddy/kayak supervision due to environmental risk factors.
evidenceCatalogue.limitations: Advisory guidelines rather than randomized controlled trials.
supportedClaims: Open-water familiarity and conditional safety practices.

coachingDerivedDecisions.description: Establishment of a 12-week duration for Half Ironman training plans.
coachingDerivedDecisions.rationale: Assumes an athlete entering with a stable baseline can peak effectively within 12 weeks of structured specific periodization.
coachingDerivedDecisions.evidenceContext: General periodization principles applied to recreational multisport training.
coachingDerivedDecisions.userFacingDisclosure: Plan duration is a coaching heuristic based on typical athlete availability and adaptation timelines.

coachingDerivedDecisions.description: Establishment of a 16-week duration for full Ironman training plans.
coachingDerivedDecisions.rationale: Full distance endurance preparation requires extended volume accumulation and multi-week peak cycles.
coachingDerivedDecisions.evidenceContext: Ultra-endurance coaching standards for first-time and intermediate finishers.
coachingDerivedDecisions.userFacingDisclosure: 16-week duration is designed to safely ramp volume for endurance completion.

coachingDerivedDecisions.description: Structuring plans into Base, Build, Peak/Race-Specific, Taper, and Race phases.
coachingDerivedDecisions.rationale: Classical linear and undulating periodization models optimize physiological adaptations.
coachingDerivedDecisions.userFacingDisclosure: Phase structures organize training load into logical progression and recovery blocks.

coachingDerivedDecisions.description: Placement of recovery weeks every third or fourth week.
coachingDerivedDecisions.rationale: Allows systemic fatigue dissipation and supercompensation of physiological adaptations.
coachingDerivedDecisions.evidenceContext: Overreaching management literature in endurance sports.
coachingDerivedDecisions.userFacingDisclosure: Recovery weeks are scheduled periodically to absorb accumulated fatigue.

coachingDerivedDecisions.description: Sequencing key long endurance sessions on weekends.
coachingDerivedDecisions.rationale: Matches traditional recreational athlete availability while respecting appropriate spacing.
coachingDerivedDecisions.evidenceContext: Practical lifestyle integration for recreational triathletes.
coachingDerivedDecisions.userFacingDisclosure: Long workouts are placed on weekends for schedule convenience.

coachingDerivedDecisions.description: Exact repetition and duration structure for threshold and tempo intervals.
coachingDerivedDecisions.rationale: Balances time-in-zone requirements with recovery capacity.
coachingDerivedDecisions.userFacingDisclosure: Interval structures are selected to stimulate aerobic power without excessive musculoskeletal stress.

coachingDerivedDecisions.description: Combining specific discipline workouts within weekly microcycles.
coachingDerivedDecisions.rationale: Ensures frequency across swim, bike, and run without exceeding safe daily stress limits.
coachingDerivedDecisions.userFacingDisclosure: Weekly session mixes maintain multi-discipline neural pathways.

coachingDerivedDecisions.description: Placement of strength sessions away from key priority runs and long rides.
coachingDerivedDecisions.rationale: Prevents residual neuromuscular fatigue from impairing high-priority endurance workouts.
coachingDerivedDecisions.userFacingDisclosure: Strength workouts are spaced to avoid interfering with key endurance sessions.

coachingDerivedDecisions.description: Designating specific technique or short sessions as optional.
coachingDerivedDecisions.rationale: Provides flexibility for athletes with variable recovery capacity or time constraints.
coachingDerivedDecisions.userFacingDisclosure: Optional sessions can be omitted if schedule or fatigue dictates.

coachingDerivedDecisions.description: Duration and volume reduction slope of taper weeks.
coachingDerivedDecisions.rationale: Sheds accumulated fatigue while maintaining neuromuscular readiness for race day.
coachingDerivedDecisions.userFacingDisclosure: Tapers systematically reduce volume while retaining short sharpening efforts.

coachingDerivedDecisions.description: Inclusion of selected double-session days in intermediate schedules.
coachingDerivedDecisions.rationale: Allows frequency and volume distribution without over-extending single-session durations.
coachingDerivedDecisions.userFacingDisclosure: Double-session days are used selectively to distribute training frequency.

coachingDerivedDecisions.description: Linear and wave progression of long ride and long run durations.
coachingDerivedDecisions.rationale: Builds physiological durability safely over multi-week blocks.
coachingDerivedDecisions.evidenceContext: Progressive overload principles in endurance training.
coachingDerivedDecisions.userFacingDisclosure: Long session durations progress gradually to build tissue resilience.

adaptationRules.informationShown: Missed easy sessions should be skipped to preserve subsequent training.
adaptationRules.historyPreservation: Mark session as missed without altering future schedule
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Do not attempt to make up missed easy volume.

adaptationRules.informationShown: Priority sessions carry key adaptations; choose whether to omit or adapt safely.
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Consult coaching review if multiple priority sessions are missed.

adaptationRules.informationShown: Missing a key long ride or long run requires assessing overall fatigue before rescheduling.
adaptationRules.historyPreservation: Log session as missed; flag for review
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Consult coach review before attempting to double up long sessions.

adaptationRules.informationShown: If a session is cut short due to fatigue or time, log completed duration and move on.
prohibitedAutomaticActions: Automatically adding remainder to next workout
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Do not make up unfinished minutes.

adaptationRules.informationShown: Missed training across several days requires load adjustment upon return.
prohibitedAutomaticActions: Resuming at full planned intensity immediately
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Ease back into training following multi-day interruptions.

adaptationRules.informationShown: A full missed week requires stepping back to a deload week structure upon return.
prohibitedAutomaticActions: Jumping straight back into peak load weeks
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Consult coach review to restructure plan timeline.

adaptationRules.informationShown: Extended absence requires comprehensive plan recalibration.
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Substantial time away invalidates current peak phasing.

adaptationRules.informationShown: Persistent fatigue warrants converting a training day to rest or easy active recovery.
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Prioritize recovery when systemic fatigue accumulates.

adaptationRules.informationShown: Above-the-neck symptoms suggest reducing intensity or resting completely.
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Monitor symptoms closely; avoid intense training.

adaptationRules.trigger: fever, chest symptoms or systemic illness
adaptationRules.informationShown: Systemic illness, fever, or chest symptoms require complete cessation of training and medical evaluation.
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Seek professional medical evaluation before resuming exercise.

adaptationRules.informationShown: Localized sharp pain in joints or tendons requires stopping aggravating activity and seeking professional assessment.
adaptationRules.historyPreservation: Log session interruption due to pain
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Focal pain warrants professional medical review.

adaptationRules.informationShown: If a pool is closed, substitute an easy aerobic cross-training session or reschedule swim.
Move swim training indoors to a pool or indoor trainer if open water conditions are unsafe.
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Never compromise safety for open water sessions.

adaptationRules.informationShown: Move outdoor rides indoors to a trainer during severe weather or hazardous road conditions.
prohibitedAutomaticActions: Forcing outdoor riding in hazardous weather
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Prioritize personal safety over outdoor route execution.

adaptationRules.informationShown: Changing race date requires recalculating taper and peak block positioning.
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Consult coach review to realign periodization phases.

adaptationRules.trigger: plan feels too easy or too hard
adaptationRules.informationShown: Significant mismatch in perceived exertion warrants reviewing baseline intensity metrics.
adaptationRules.escalationMessage: Evaluate underlying intensity markers before altering training load.

safetyMessages.title: Open-Water Swimming Safety
safetyMessages.message: Open-water swimming involves environmental risks including temperature, currents, and limited visibility. Swim only with supervision and verified safety conditions.

safetyMessages.title: Unsafe Water or Weather
safetyMessages.message: Avoid training in severe weather, lightning storms, or hazardous water conditions.

safetyMessages.title: Outdoor Cycling Handling
safetyMessages.message: Exercise caution, obey traffic laws, and maintain bike control during outdoor cycling sessions.

safetyMessages.title: Heat and Thermal Stress
safetyMessages.message: Monitor environmental heat and adjust intensity or hydration to prevent heat-related illness.

safetyMessages.title: Systemic Illness
safetyMessages.message: Systemic illness, fever, or chest symptoms require immediate cessation of training.

safetyMessages.title: Focal Pain
safetyMessages.message: Sharp or persistent focal pain in joints, bones, or tendons requires stopping activity.

safetyMessages.title: Excessive Fatigue
safetyMessages.message: Chronic or excessive fatigue indicates insufficient recovery and warrants training reduction.

safetyMessages.title: Fueling Tolerance
safetyMessages.message: Practice nutrition strategies during long training sessions to assess individual gastrointestinal tolerance.

safetyMessages.title: Hydration and Hyponatremia
safetyMessages.message: Avoid rigid universal fluid quotas and overhydration; drink according to thirst.

safetyMessages.title: Carbohydrate Evidence Ranges
safetyMessages.message: Carbohydrate ingestion guidelines during prolonged exercise should be tailored to individual needs.

safetyMessages.title: Gastrointestinal Training
safetyMessages.message: Train the gut progressively during long sessions to improve race-day carbohydrate absorption.

safetyMessages.title: Long-Session Duration
safetyMessages.message: Extended duration sessions increase musculoskeletal and metabolic strain; pace conservatively.

safetyMessages.title: Strength Technique
safetyMessages.message: Prioritize proper form and controlled execution during strength training sessions.

safetyMessages.title: Race Execution
safetyMessages.message: Execute race pacing conservatively to ensure successful completion across all three disciplines.

safetyMessages.title: Emergency Symptoms
safetyMessages.message: Chest pain, severe dizziness, or acute trauma require immediate emergency medical attention.

safetyMessages.title: Research-Candidate Scope
safetyMessages.message: These training plans are research candidates and do not constitute medical advice or guaranteed outcomes.

prohibitedAutomation.prohibitedBehaviour: ACWR causal prediction or hard gate
prohibitedAutomation.reason: ACWR is not a validated causal predictor of injury.
prohibitedAutomation.permittedAlternative: Monitor subjective fatigue and training load trends.

prohibitedAutomation.reason: HRV alone cannot dictate training adaptations.
prohibitedAutomation.permittedAlternative: Combine subjective wellness with HRV trends.

prohibitedAutomation.reason: BMI does not determine athletic capability or safety.
Recovery requirements vary individually rather than by sex.
A universal 10% rule lacks individual physiological validity.
The neck check is not a medical clearance tool.
prohibitedAutomation.permittedAlternative: Seek professional medical evaluation for illness.

prohibitedAutomation.reason: Stacking missed workouts increases injury risk.
prohibitedAutomation.permittedAlternative: Omit missed easy sessions and proceed safely.

prohibitedAutomation.prohibitedBehaviour: Automatic relinking or rewriting of completed history
prohibitedAutomation.reason: Completed training history must remain immutable.
Archived or deleted content must not be automatically restored.
All sessions must derive from accepted session library.

prohibitedAutomation.prohibitedBehaviour: Invented sets, repetitions, loads or rest
prohibitedAutomation.reason: Do not fabricate interval structures outside catalogue.
Universal quotas ignore individual sweat rates and conditions.
prohibitedAutomation.permittedAlternative: Drink according to thirst and individual fueling plans.

prohibitedAutomation.reason: Endurance training carries inherent uncertainty and risk.
prohibitedAutomation.permittedAlternative: Provide realistic scoping and safety disclosures.
